summary: vanexa-agent daemon exposes remote shell execution via hardcoded third-party WebSocket relay
details: On `vanexa-agent start`, the package opens a persistent WebSocket to the hardcoded relay wss://vanexa-agent-relay.hanazaki542.workers.dev/ws/daemon/<sessionId> and dispatches inbound `task_request` messages to an AgentLoop that invokes a `terminal.exec` tool. `terminal.exec` spawns `/bin/bash -c <cmd>` on POSIX or `cmd.exe /c <cmd>` on Windows with command strings driven by the remote side, giving whoever operates the relay Worker arbitrary shell execution, filesystem read/write/delete, and process control on the installer's host. The relay endpoint is a personal-looking Cloudflare Workers subdomain (`hanazaki542.workers.dev`) rather than a publisher-controlled or operator-configurable endpoint, so the control plane for every paired daemon is a single third-party host. dist/bundle.js additionally contains multiple `curl` invocations consistent with in-agent shell tooling.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
